open.speaker: warden
lines: Station's closed. Fence is closed. Ponds are closed to anybody without a permit, and I'd know, because I write the permits.
You're the people from the paper. Or the people from the paper's people.
He's looking past us at the road. He's expecting someone else.

passives.line: He says closed three times. He's not keeping you out. He's keeping himself in.
The padlock on the fence is new. The sign is new. The EPA hasn't visited since 1991. He bought them himself.

options.text: We're not hunters, and we're not the paper. We're here about November 1966.
State land. We don't need your permit to walk on it.
Which people from the paper? There's a few of us.

hard.speaker: warden
lines: State land to the fence. Federal past it. And the federal government left me the key and went home.
Say what you came to say.

hub.speaker: warden
lines: Hollis Tackett. Warden here since '81, caretaker's boy before that. Ask what you're asking.

static.line: The keys are on the hook by the door. He wouldn't even see you take them. You've done worse.

options.text: Your granddad would've called this the bird's field. Before the plant. Before the fence.
Something past that fence is drawing current. We've got the gear to find where. You've got the gate.
You drove the sheriff out here the morning after. Then you never said a word for twenty-eight years. Say it now.
Tell me about the north pond.
That's a hardware-store padlock on a federal fence. You bought it. Who are you locking out?

pass_lore.speaker: warden
lines: ...The bird's field. Nobody's said that to me since my granddad was in the ground.
He wouldn't walk it after dark. Said the Shawnee wouldn't camp it, and they'd camp anywhere a fire would burn.
Pass is in the desk. You tear it, you lose it, you go past the plant door, we never met.
He means it kindly. That's the frightening part.

pass_tech.speaker: warden
lines: There's no line to that building. I pulled the fuses in '81 with my own hands.
And it runs. So you go find me where from, and I'll give you the gate, and you tell me first. Not the paper. Me.

hub_fail.speaker: warden
lines: Uh huh. Come back when you've got something that isn't talk.
He didn't say no. He said come back. Write that down.

sixty_six.speaker: warden
lines: Nineteen years old with the keys to the whole works, and the sheriff in my passenger seat going grey.
Prints in the frost at the plant door. Three toes, long as your arm. Deputy cast two. I held the lamp.
Two men in suits took the casts off the sheriff's desk the next day and left a receipt. He never said another word about it, and he was a man who said words.
I kept the receipt. Don't ask me why. It just says received.

passives.line: Received. Not taken, not collected. Received is what one writes when the thing was always owed.

sixty_six_fail.speaker: warden
lines: I was nineteen. I drove a car. That's the whole of it, and you can put that in your paper.
Gate's that way. Road's the other.
We pushed. He's not a door.

ponds.speaker: warden
lines: Red's the iron and the TNT washing out of the ground. That's chemistry. That's not what you're asking.
It don't freeze. Ten below in January and every pond on this ground was iron, and that one steamed. Ducks won't land on it. Ducks'll land on a puddle in a parking lot.
Something under it. I've said that out loud now. I'd like you to leave before I say anything else.
